notes: Nonnumeric input reaches C's safety response byte-for-byte across the focused seed matrix (R1/R2/R5e).
Numeric input outside every real zone reaches C's exact unknown-zone response, including state cleanup (R1/R2/R4/R5e).
An empty argument selects the actor's current room and emits the C REDIT main menu (R1/R2/R5e).
A valid room enters the descriptor-owned editor and routes later lines through its menu state, matching C (R1/R2/R4/R5e).
Invalid main-menu input preserves C's contiguous error/menu response (R1/R2/R5e).
Room description editing uses the C improved editor, including help, blank input, save, and abort return behavior (R1/R3/R4/R5e).
Room flag menu formatting, invalid selection, bit toggle, and return path match C (R1/R2/R4/R5e).
Sector menu and selection preserve C's table, prompt, and state transition (R1/R2/R4/R5e).
Exit identity, target validation, description editor, keywords, key, door flags, purge, and menu prompts match the C path (R1/R2/R4/R5e).
Extra-description creation, completion gating, editor abort/save, and removal behavior match the C linked-list path (R1/R2/R4/R5e).
Room name/description copy preserves the C source-room lookup and return menu (R1/R4/R5e).
Existing-room script name/flag editing follows C's live shallow-script authority and menu transitions; new-room script assignment remains C-rejected (R1/R2/R4/R5e).
Room-editor start/stop activity reaches the co-located observer with C's actor-excluding audience behavior (R1/R3/R5e).
The registered command carries C's POS_DEAD and LVL_IMMORT entry gate (R1/R2/R5e).
Working edits remain descriptor-local until C's save confirmation, and abort leaves the live room unchanged (R1/R4/R5e).
A new room commits to the live parsed world, is written in C .wld form, and is parsed back after a restart boundary (R1/R4/R5e).
Disconnect cleanup drops an active room string buffer without committing it or leaving PLR_WRITING set (R1/R4/R5e).

A live external room write remains visible while the separate REDIT working copy is later discarded (the HTTP admin write path this originally named was removed in PR #1502; the scenario now drives the same concurrent write through the game layer); publication uses the same locked copy-on-write boundary (R1/R3/R4/R5e).
Concurrent REDIT publication, web-admin room writes, script writes, and lock-free readers complete without race reports while each snapshot remains structurally valid (R1/R3/R4/R5e).
OLC menus embed get_char_cols ANSI (grn/nrm/cyn/yel) at color level >= 2; keep-ansi compares the raw escape bytes themselves, with creation answering Y to the ANSI question (R1/R5a).
With color off every menu byte is plain; keep-ansi proves the port neither drops nor invents escape bytes at color level 0 (R1/R4).
Concurrent redit entry admits exactly one editor through an atomic reservation; disconnect and clean-quit paths both release it (R1/R3).

Routine door EX_ writes publish per-room copy-on-write without the structural rebuild; runtime door state survives later structural commits; cost measured on the real ~10k-room world in world_redit_bench_test.go (R1/R3/R5a).

A saved zone survives an actual fresh boot (ParseWorld + NewWorld, the cmd/server path); edited name, description, exit target/keywords/key/door flags, and extra desc are revisited through a new session's look state (R1/R4/R5f).
